title.zh: 卷373 列傳一百六十 宗室奕山 隆文 宗室奕经 文蔚 特依顺 余步雲
title.en: Volume 373 Biographies 160: Zong Shiyishan, Long Wen, Zong Shiyijing, Wen Wei, Te Yi Shun, Yu Buyun
title.raw: 卷373 列傳一百六十 宗室奕山 隆文 宗室奕经 文蔚 特依顺 余步雲

sentences.zh: =宗室奕山=宗室奕山，恂郡王允禵四世孫，隸鑲藍旗。

translations.literal: Yi Shan, Imperial Clansman — Yi Shan, an imperial clansman, was a fourth-generation descendant of Prince Xun Yunli and belonged to the Bordered Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Shan, Imperial Clansman — Yi Shan, a member of the imperial clan, was a fourth-generation descendant of Prince Xun Yunli and was registered in the Bordered Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 授乾清門侍衛。

translations.literal: He was appointed an attendant of the Gate of Heavenly Purity.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed an attendant at the Gate of Heavenly Purity.

sentences.zh: 道光七年，從征喀什噶爾，擢頭等侍衛、御前行走。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Daoguang, he joined the campaign against Kashgar and was promoted to First Class Bodyguard with the privilege of imperial escort duty.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of the Daoguang reign, he took part in the expedition against Kashgar and was promoted to First Class Bodyguard with the right to attend the emperor on duty.

sentences.zh: 歷伊犁領隊大臣、參贊大臣。

translations.literal: He served successively as Brigade General of Ili and as Adviser Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as Brigade General of Ili and as Adviser Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十八年，授伊犁將軍。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was appointed General of Ili.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was appointed military governor of Ili.

sentences.zh: 二十年，偕副都統關福赴塔什圖畢治墾務，闢田十六萬四千馀畝，奏請置回千戶及五品伯克以下官。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, together with Vice Commander-in-Chief Guan Fu he went to Tashitubi to oversee land reclamation, opening more than 164,000 mu of fields, and memorialized to establish Hui thousand-household posts and officials from fifth-rank bakhshi downward.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he went with Vice Commander-in-Chief Guan Fu to Tashitubi to direct reclamation work, opened more than 164,000 mu of farmland, and memorialized the throne to set up Hui thousand-household units and officials from fifth-rank bakhshi down.

sentences.zh: 召授正白旗領侍衛內大臣、御前大臣。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Grand Minister of the Attendant Guard of the Plain White Banner and Imperial Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to court and appointed Grand Minister of the Attendant Guard of the Plain White Banner and Imperial Minister.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，命為靖逆將軍，督師廣東，尚書​​隆文、提督楊芳為參贊副之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was ordered to serve as Pacification General, commanding troops in Guangdong, with Minister Long Wen and Provincial Military Commander Yang Fang as deputy advisers.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he was named Pacification General to command the Guangdong front, with Minister Long Wen and Provincial Military Commander Yang Fang as his deputies.

sentences.zh: 時英兵已陷虎門，楊芳先至，聽美利堅人居間，乞許通商，被嚴斥，促奕山速赴軍。

translations.literal: At that time the English army had already taken Humen. Yang Fang arrived first and, heeding American intermediaries, petitioned to allow trade; he was sternly rebuked and Yishan was urged to hurry to the front.
translations.idiomatic: By then the British had already captured Humen. Yang Fang reached Guangdong first and, taking advice from American go-betweens, asked permission to resume trade; he was sharply rebuked, and Yishan was ordered to reach the army without delay.

sentences.zh: 三月，抵廣州。

translations.literal: In the third month he reached Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he arrived at Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 英艦橫亙省河，奕山問計於林則徐，則徐議先遣洋商設法羈縻，俾英艦暫退；

translations.literal: English warships lay across the provincial river. Yishan asked Lin Zexu for a plan; Lin proposed first sending foreign merchants to negotiate restraint so the English ships might temporarily withdraw;
translations.idiomatic: British warships blocked the provincial river. Yishan sought Lin Zexu's counsel; Lin urged that foreign merchants first be used to stall the enemy so the British fleet might pull back for a time;

sentences.zh: 塞河道，積沙囊於岸以御砲，然後以守為攻。

translations.literal: block the river channel, pile sandbags on the banks to ward off cannon fire, and then take defense as offense.
translations.idiomatic: then block the channel, heap sandbags along the banks against artillery, and only afterward turn defense into attack.

sentences.zh: 奕山不能用，且自琦善撤防，舊儲木椿鉅石皆為敵移去，時以杉板小船游弋以誘我師。

translations.literal: Yishan could not adopt this. Moreover, since Qi Shan had withdrawn the defenses, the old stores of wooden piles and massive stones had all been removed by the enemy, who now cruised in fir-plank skiffs to lure our army.
translations.idiomatic: Yishan would not follow this advice. After Qi Shan had stripped the defenses, the enemy had carried off the old stockpiles of piles and boulders, and now sent out light fir boats to bait our forces.

sentences.zh: 楊芳主持重，以募勇未集，不欲浪戰。

translations.literal: Yang Fang favored caution; the recruited braves were not yet assembled, and he did not wish to fight recklessly.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fang urged restraint: the hired militia were not yet gathered, and he did not want a rash battle.

sentences.zh: 奕山初亦然之，既而惑於左右言，欲僥倖一試，芳止之不可。

translations.literal: Yishan at first agreed, but then, misled by advisers around him, he wished to try his luck once; Fang could not dissuade him.
translations.idiomatic: Yishan at first agreed, but then his entourage persuaded him to gamble on one stroke of luck; Fang could not hold him back.

sentences.zh: 夜進兵，乘風毀七艘，報捷，詰旦乃知誤焚民舟，而英兵大至，連舟抵城下；

translations.literal: At night they advanced; riding the wind they destroyed seven vessels and reported victory—but at dawn they learned they had mistakenly burned civilian boats, while the English army arrived in force and linked their ships under the city walls;
translations.idiomatic: They attacked by night and, with the wind behind them, burned seven craft and reported a victory; at daybreak they found they had set fire to civilian boats, while the main British force came up and moored in a line beneath the walls;

sentences.zh: 禦於河南，互有殺傷，遂閉城。

translations.literal: They fought them off south of the river with casualties on both sides, then shut the gates.
translations.idiomatic: They fought south of the river with losses on both sides, then closed the city gates.

sentences.zh: 敵以輪船襲泥城，副將岱昌等聞砲先遁，毀師船六十有奇，城外東西砲台並陷。

translations.literal: The enemy used steam warships to attack Nicheng. Deputy Commander Dai Chang and others fled at the sound of cannon; more than sixty war junks were destroyed, and the eastern and western batteries outside the city all fell.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy sent steamers against Nicheng. Deputy Commander Dai Chang and others fled at the first cannonade; more than sixty government war junks were lost, and the batteries east and west of the city were taken.

sentences.zh: 英兵進踞後山四方砲台，奕山居貢院，砲火及焉，軍民惶懼，乃遣廣州知府餘保純出城見義律議息兵。

translations.literal: The English army seized the four-sided battery on the rear hill. Yishan lodged in the examination hall; cannon fire reached there; soldiers and civilians were terrified, and he sent Guangzhou Prefect Yu Baochun out to meet Elliot and negotiate a ceasefire.
translations.idiomatic: British troops occupied the four-sided battery on the rear hill. Yishan stayed in the examination compound while shells fell around him; soldiers and townspeople panicked, and he sent Guangzhou Prefect Yu Baochun out to Elliot to discuss a truce.

sentences.zh: 義律索煙價千二百萬，美商居間減其半，並許給香港全島，英兵乃退。

translations.literal: Elliot demanded twelve million in opium indemnity; American merchants mediated and halved it, and the whole island of Hong Kong was also granted; the English army then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Elliot demanded twelve million taels for destroyed opium; American merchants intervened and cut the sum in half, and the entire island of Hong Kong was also conceded before the British withdrew.

sentences.zh: 奕山偕隆文先退，屯距城六十里小金山，諱敗為勝。

translations.literal: Yishan and Long Wen withdrew first and encamped at Little Golden Hill sixty li from the city, concealing defeat as victory.
translations.idiomatic: Yishan and Long Wen pulled back first and camped at Little Golden Hill, sixty li from the city, passing off defeat as victory.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「義律窮蹙乞撫，照舊通商，改償費為追交商欠，由粵海關及籓運兩庫給之。

translations.literal: In a memorial he stated: "Elliot, hard pressed, begged for pacification; trade was to continue as before; the compensation was to be changed to recovery of commercial debts, payable from the Guangdong Maritime Customs and the grain-transport treasuries."
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he wrote: "Elliot, driven to extremity, sued for peace; trade would continue as before; the indemnity would be recast as collection of merchants' debts, to be paid from the Guangdong customs and the grain-transport treasuries."

sentences.zh: 」宣宗覽奏，以夷情恭順，詔允所請。

translations.literal: The Emperor read the memorial, deemed the foreigners respectful and compliant, and issued an edict approving the request.
translations.idiomatic: The Daoguang Emperor read the report, took the foreigners to be submissive, and approved what was asked.

sentences.zh: 閩浙總督顏伯燾迭疏劾其欺罔，下廣西巡撫梁章鉅察奏，乃得其狀，報聞。

translations.literal: Governor-General of Fujian and Zhejiang Yan Bozhe repeatedly memorialized impeaching him for deception; the Guangxi Governor Liang Zhangju was ordered to investigate and report, and the true situation was thereby established and reported to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Bozhe, governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang, repeatedly impeached him for fraud; Liang Zhangju, governor of Guangxi, was ordered to investigate, and the facts came out in his report.

sentences.zh: 英人既得賂於粵，移兵犯閩、浙。

translations.literal: After the English had exacted payment in Guangdong, they shifted troops to attack Fujian and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Once the British had secured their payment in Guangdong, they moved their forces against Fujian and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 奕山等始收回大黃、獵德、虎門諸砲台，填塞省河。

translations.literal: Yishan and others then recovered the Dahuang, Liede, Humen, and other batteries and blocked the provincial river.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did Yishan and his colleagues retake the batteries at Dahuang, Liede, Humen, and elsewhere, and block the provincial river.

sentences.zh: 鄉民於義律未退時，困之三元里，餘保純趨救始得出。

translations.literal: While Elliot had not yet withdrawn, local militia cornered him at Sanyuanli; only when Yu Baochun rushed to rescue did he escape.
translations.idiomatic: Before Elliot had left, local militia trapped him at Sanyuanli; he got away only when Yu Baochun hurried out to extricate him.

sentences.zh: 於是團練日盛，中外皆言粵民可用，遂撤客軍，改募練勇。

translations.literal: Militia training then flourished daily; at home and abroad all said the Guangdong people could be relied on, so foreign troops were withdrawn and local militia were recruited instead.
translations.idiomatic: Militia drill grew stronger by the day; officials at court and in the provinces alike said the Cantonese could be trusted, foreign detachments were sent home, and local militia were enlisted in their place.

sentences.zh: 迭詔趣奕山等規复香港，實不能戰，惟屢疏陳颶風漂沒敵船，毀香港蓬藔，藉修砲台未竣、造船未就為詞，以塞嚴詔。

translations.literal: Edicts repeatedly urged Yishan and others to plan recovery of Hong Kong, but they were in fact unable to fight; they only repeatedly memorialized that typhoons had sunk enemy ships and destroyed Hong Kong huts, citing unfinished battery repairs and uncompleted shipbuilding as excuses to satisfy stern orders.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated edicts pressed Yishan and his colleagues to recover Hong Kong, but they could not really fight; they kept reporting that storms had sunk British ships and wrecked Hong Kong's sheds, pleading unfinished batteries and unfinished ships to answer the emperor's demands.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，英人撤義律回國，以濮鼎查代之，大舉犯浙江、江蘇。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year the English recalled Elliot and replaced him with Pottinger, launching a major offensive against Zhejiang and Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year the British recalled Elliot and sent Pottinger in his place, then mounted a large campaign against Zhejiang and Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 詔斥奕山陳奏欺詐，嚴議褫御前大臣、領侍衛內大臣、左都御史，仍留漢軍都統任。

translations.literal: An edict rebuked Yishan for fraudulent memorials and ordered severe punishment: stripping him of Imperial Minister, Grand Minister of the Attendant Guard, and Censor-in-Chief, while retaining his post as Commander-in-Chief of the Han Eight Banners.
translations.idiomatic: An edict condemned Yishan's deceitful reports and ordered severe discipline: he lost his posts as Imperial Minister, Grand Minister of the Attendant Guard, and Censor-in-Chief, but kept command of the Han Eight Banners.

sentences.zh: 及和議定，追論援粵失機，褫職治罪，論大辟，圈禁宗人府空室。

translations.literal: When peace was settled, they pursued the charge of failing to reinforce Guangdong in time: he was stripped of office and sentenced, condemned to death, and confined in an empty room in the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: After the peace treaty, he was prosecuted for missing the chance to aid Guangdong: stripped of rank, tried, sentenced to death, and imprisoned in an empty cell of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，釋之，予二等侍衛，充和闐辦事大臣，調伊犁參贊大臣，署將軍。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was released, granted Second Class Bodyguard, appointed Commissioner in Khotan, transferred to Ili as Adviser Commissioner, and acted as General.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he was freed, given the rank of Second Class Bodyguard, made commissioner in Khotan, transferred to Ili as adviser commissioner, and served as acting general.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，調葉爾羌參贊大臣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he was transferred to be Adviser Commissioner at Yarkand.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year he was posted as adviser commissioner at Yarkand.

sentences.zh: 安集延布魯特、回匪入邊，圍喀什噶爾、英吉沙爾，命陝甘總督布彥泰督師討之，奕山為副，連破賊於科科熱依瓦特及蘇噶特布拉克，賊遁走。

translations.literal: Kokand Kirghiz and Hui rebels crossed the border and besieged Kashgar and Yengisar. Shaan-Gan Governor-General Buyantai was ordered to command the campaign; Yishan served as deputy and repeatedly defeated the rebels at Kokoreyivat and Sugatbulak, and the rebels fled.
translations.idiomatic: Kokand Kirghiz and Muslim rebels raided the frontier and besieged Kashgar and Yengisar. Buyantai, governor-general of Shaanxi and Gansu, was ordered to lead the punitive force with Yishan as his second; they beat the rebels at Kokoreyivat and Sugatbulak in succession, and the enemy withdrew.

sentences.zh: 論功，封二等鎮國將軍，賜雙眼花翎。

translations.literal: For merit he was enfeoffed as Second-rank Defender Prince of the State and granted the double-eyed peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was made Second-rank Defender Prince of the State and awarded the double-eyed peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 尋授內閣學士，調伊犁參贊大臣，兼鑲黃旗蒙古都統。

translations.literal: Soon after he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat, transferred to Ili as Adviser Commissioner, and concurrently made Commander of the Mongol Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made a grand secretary, returned to Ili as adviser commissioner, and also served as commander of the Mongol Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，授伊犁將軍。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was appointed General of Ili.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he was again appointed military governor of Ili.

sentences.zh: 俄羅斯遣使至伊犁，請於伊犁、塔爾巴哈台、喀什噶爾三處通商，詔允其二，惟喀什噶爾不許。

translations.literal: Russia sent envoys to Ili requesting trade at Ili, Tarbagatai, and Kashgar; an edict approved two of these but forbade Kashgar.
translations.idiomatic: Russia sent envoys to Ili asking to open trade at Ili, Tarbagatai, and Kashgar; the court allowed two of the three but refused Kashgar.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，俄人復固請，仍拒之，偕參贊布彥泰與定伊塔通商章程十七條。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng the Russians again pressed the request and were again refused; together with Adviser Commissioner Buyantai he fixed the seventeen articles of the Ili-Tarbagatai trade regulations.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianfeng the Russians asked again and were turned down again; with Adviser Commissioner Buyantai he drew up the seventeen articles governing trade at Ili and Tarbagatai.

sentences.zh: 祭酒勝保疏論當仿恰克圖通商舊例，限以時日、人數。

translations.literal: Libationer Sheng Bao memorialized that the old Kiakhta trade precedent should be followed, limiting days and numbers of persons.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Bao, libationer of the Imperial Academy, argued in a memorial that trade should follow the Kiakhta precedent, with limits on season and numbers of traders.

sentences.zh: 奕山議：「撫馭外夷以信為主，既已議定章程，旋改必有藉口。

translations.literal: Yishan argued: "In managing foreigners faith is paramount; once regulations have been agreed, to alter them at once will certainly give them a pretext."
translations.idiomatic: Yishan replied: "In dealing with foreigners, good faith comes first; once regulations are settled, any sudden change will only give them an excuse."

sentences.zh: 」如所請行。

translations.literal: It was carried out as he requested.
translations.idiomatic: The court acted as he advised.

sentences.zh: 累授內大臣、御前大臣，仍留將軍任。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly appointed Inner Minister and Imperial Minister while retaining the post of General.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to Inner Minister and Imperial Minister while keeping his post as military governor.

sentences.zh: 五年，調黑龍江將軍。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to be General of Heilongjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was transferred to military governor of Heilongjiang.

sentences.zh: 時俄羅斯以分界為名，欲得黑龍江、松花江左岸地，遣艦入精奇里江，建屋於霍爾托庫、圖勒密、布雅里。

translations.literal: At that time Russia, under the name of demarcation, sought the lands on the left banks of the Amur and Sungari, sent ships into the Zeya River, and built houses at Huo'ertoku, Tulemi, and Buyali.
translations.idiomatic: Russia, under cover of boundary talks, wanted the left banks of the Amur and Sungari, sent warships up the Zeya, and built houses at Huo'ertoku, Tulemi, and Buyali.

sentences.zh: 奕山疏陳陽撫陰防之策。

translations.literal: Yishan memorialized a policy of open conciliation and covert defense.
translations.idiomatic: Yishan proposed in a memorial to placate the Russians openly while guarding against them in secret.

sentences.zh: 七年，俄使請入京，拒不許。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the Russian envoy asked to enter the capital and was refused.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year a Russian envoy asked to go to Beijing and was turned away.

sentences.zh: 八年，俄人偕英、法、美三國合兵犯天津。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the Russians joined England, France, and the United States in a combined attack on Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Russia marched with Britain, France, and the United States against Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 三國窺商利，而俄志在邊地，於是俄使木里裴岳幅至愛琿，堅請畫界，奕山允自額爾古納河口循黑龍江至松花江左岸之地盡屬之俄。

translations.literal: The three powers eyed commercial profit, while Russia's aim was frontier territory. The Russian envoy Muraviev then came to Aigun and pressed hard for demarcation; Yishan agreed that all land from the Argun mouth along the Amur to the left bank of the Sungari should belong to Russia.
translations.idiomatic: Britain, France, and America were after trade gains, but Russia wanted land. Muraviev came to Aigun and insisted on a boundary line; Yishan conceded everything from the Argun mouth along the Amur to the left bank of the Sungari to Russia.

sentences.zh: 俄使知奕山昧於地勢，駐兵黑龍江口，复索綏芬河、烏蘇里江地，奕山懾其兵威，勿能抗，疏稱未許，然已告俄使可比照海口等處辦理。

translations.literal: The Russian envoy, knowing Yishan was ignorant of the terrain, stationed troops at the mouth of the Amur and again demanded the lands of the Suifen and Ussuri rivers. Yishan, awed by their military power, could not resist; in a memorial he said he had not agreed, yet he had already told the Russian envoy it might be handled like the treaty ports.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that Yishan did not know the ground, Muraviev camped troops at the Amur mouth and demanded the Suifen and Ussuri basins as well. Intimidated, Yishan could not refuse outright; he reported that he had not consented, but had already told the Russians it could be treated like the open ports.

sentences.zh: 逾年，與俄使會於愛琿，定約三條，鑱滿、蒙、漢三體字為界碑。

translations.literal: The following year he met the Russian envoy at Aigun, fixed a treaty of three articles, and carved boundary markers in Manchu, Mongol, and Chinese.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he met the Russian envoy at Aigun, signed a three-article treaty, and set up boundary stones inscribed in Manchu, Mongol, and Chinese.

sentences.zh: 大理寺少卿殷兆鏞劾奕山：「以邊地五千馀裡，藉稱閒曠，不候諭旨，拱手授人，始既輕諾，繼复受人所製，無能轉圜。

translations.literal: Vice President of the Court of Judicial Review Yin Zhaoyong impeached Yishan: "More than five thousand li of frontier, on the pretext that it was idle waste land, without awaiting imperial instruction he handed it over with open hands; at first he lightly promised, then again fell into another's design and could not recover."
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhaoyong, vice president of the Court of Judicial Review, impeached Yishan: "He gave away more than five thousand li of frontier, calling it empty land, without waiting for the throne's order; he promised too easily at first, then let the Russians dictate terms and could not undo the damage."

sentences.zh: 」詔切責之，革職留任；

translations.literal: An edict sharply rebuked him and stripped his office while retaining him in his post;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked him sharply, removed his rank but kept him at his post;

sentences.zh: 又以縱俄艦往黑龍江不之阻，褫御前大臣，召回京。

translations.literal: and again, for allowing Russian ships up the Amur without blocking them, stripped him of Imperial Minister and recalled him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: and, because he had let Russian ships sail up the Amur without stopping them, removed him as Imperial Minister and recalled him to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 十一年，聯軍在京定約，因奕山前議，自烏蘇里江口而南逾興凱湖，至綏芬河、瑚布圖河口，复沿琿春河達圖們江口，以東盡與俄人，語具邦交志。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the allied armies fixed a treaty in the capital; because of Yishan's earlier agreement, from the Ussuri mouth south across Lake Khanka to the Suifen and Hunchun river mouths, then along the Hunchun River to the Tumen mouth, all to the east was given to Russia—the details are in the Treaties section.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the allied powers signed a treaty in Beijing; relying on Yishan's earlier concessions, everything east of a line from the Ussuri mouth south across Lake Khanka to the Suifen and Hunchun rivers, then along the Hunchun to the Tumen, went to Russia, as recorded in the diplomatic annals.

sentences.zh: 尋复御前大臣，補正紅旗蒙古都統。

translations.literal: Soon after he was restored as Imperial Minister and appointed Commander of the Mongol Plain Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Imperial Minister again and given command of the Mongol Plain Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 同治中，封一等鎮國將軍，授內大臣。

translations.literal: During the Tongzhi reign he was enfeoffed as First-rank Defender Prince of the State and appointed Inner Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tongzhi emperor he was raised to First-rank Defender Prince of the State and made an Inner Minister.

sentences.zh: 以疾罷。

translations.literal: He retired on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Illness forced his retirement.

sentences.zh: 光緒四年，卒，諡莊簡。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Guangxu he died and was given the posthumous title Zhuangjian.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Guangxu and was posthumously titled Zhuangjian.

sentences.zh: 子載鷟，理籓院侍郎。

translations.literal: His son Zaizhuo served as Vice President of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zaizhuo became vice president of the Court of Colonial Affairs.

sentences.zh: 載鷟子溥瀚，鑲黃旗蒙古副都統；

translations.literal: Zaizhuo's son Puhan was Deputy Commander of the Mongol Bordered Yellow Banner;
translations.idiomatic: Zaizhuo's son Puhan served as deputy commander of the Mongol Bordered Yellow Banner;

sentences.zh: 孫毓照，一等奉國將軍。

translations.literal: his grandson Yuzhao was a First-rank Supporter Prince of the State.
translations.idiomatic: and his grandson Yuzhao held the rank of First-rank Supporter Prince of the State.

sentences.zh: =隆文=隆文，伊爾根覺羅氏，滿洲正紅旗人。

translations.literal: Long Wen — Long Wen, of the Irgen Gioro clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Long Wen — Long Wen, of the Irgen Gioro clan, belonged to the Manchu Plain Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十三年進士，選庶吉士，散館改刑部主事。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Jiaqing he passed the metropolitan examination, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and after leaving the academy was made a principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the thirteenth year of Jiaqing, entered the Hanlin as a probationer, and on leaving the academy became a principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 坐事罷職，捐复，授翰林院侍講。

translations.literal: He was dismissed for an offense, bought reinstatement, and was appointed Hanlin Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Dismissed after an offense, he bought his way back and was made a Hanlin reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 累擢內閣學士。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 道光中，充駐藏大臣。

translations.literal: During the Daoguang reign he served as Resident Commissioner in Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: Under Daoguang he served as the imperial commissioner in Tibet.

sentences.zh: 歷吏部、戶部侍郎，左都御史，刑部、兵部尚書，軍機大臣。

translations.literal: He served successively as Vice Minister of Personnel and Revenue, Censor-in-Chief, Minister of Punishments and War, and Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice minister of Personnel and Revenue, censor-in-chief, minister of Punishments and War, and member of the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 屢奉使出讞獄。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly sent out on imperial commission to try capital cases.
translations.idiomatic: He was often dispatched on imperial orders to hear capital cases.

sentences.zh: 偕奕山督師廣東，意不相合，甫至，病，憂憤而卒，諡端毅。

translations.literal: He accompanied Yishan to command troops in Guangdong; their views did not agree. He had only just arrived when he fell ill and died in grief and anger; his posthumous title was Duanyi.
translations.idiomatic: He went with Yishan to command in Guangdong, but they did not see eye to eye. He had barely arrived when illness and distress killed him; he was posthumously titled Duanyi.

sentences.zh: =宗室奕經=宗室奕經，成親王永瑆孫，貝勒綿懿子，承繼循郡王允璋後，隸鑲紅旗。

translations.literal: Yijing, Imperial Clansman — Yijing, an imperial clansman, was a grandson of Prince Cheng Yongxing, son of Prince Mianyi, succeeded to the line of Prince Xun Yunzhang, and belonged to the Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Yijing, Imperial Clansman — Yijing was a grandson of Prince Cheng Yongxing and son of Prince Mianyi; he succeeded the line of Prince Xun Yunzhang and was registered in the Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 授乾清門侍衛，歷奉宸院卿、內閣學士，兼副都統、護軍統​​領。

translations.literal: He was appointed attendant of the Gate of Heavenly Purity, served successively as Director of the Imperial Household Department and Grand Secretary, and concurrently held the posts of Vice Commander-in-Chief and Commander of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He became an attendant at the Gate of Heavenly Purity, then director of the Imperial Household Department and grand secretary, while also serving as vice commander-in-chief and commander of the guards.

sentences.zh: 道光三年，坐失察惇親王肩輿擅入神武中門，褫兼職，留內閣學士任。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daoguang, for failure to supervise when Prince Dun's sedan chair entered the Central Gate of the Divine Martiality without authorization, his concurrent posts were stripped while he retained the post of Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Daoguang he was punished for lax oversight when Prince Dun's sedan entered the Central Gate of the Divine Martiality without permission; he lost his concurrent offices but kept his grand secretary post.

sentences.zh: 五年，遷兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was made vice minister of War.

sentences.zh: 十年，從征喀什噶爾回匪，事平回京，歷吏部、戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he joined the campaign against the Kashgar Hui rebels; when the affair was settled he returned to the capital and served successively as Vice Minister of Personnel and Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he took part in the campaign against the Kashgar rebels; after peace he returned to Beijing and served as vice minister of Personnel and Revenue in turn.

sentences.zh: 十四年，出為黑龍江將軍。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he went out as General of Heilongjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was posted as military governor of Heilongjiang.

sentences.zh: 十六年，召授吏部尚書，兼步軍統領。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was summoned and appointed Minister of Personnel, concurrently Commander of the Metropolitan Infantry.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was recalled and made minister of Personnel, with concurrent command of the metropolitan infantry.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was made Associate Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he was appointed associate grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 英兵犯浙江，定海、鎮海及寧波府城相繼陷，裕謙死事，命為揚威將軍，督師往剿，都統哈哴阿、提督胡超為參贊，尋易侍郎文蔚、都統特依順副之。

translations.literal: When the English army attacked Zhejiang, Dinghai, Zhenhai, and the prefectural city of Ningbo fell in succession and Yu Qian died in service, he was ordered to serve as Campaign General, commanding troops to suppress the enemy, with Banner Commander Ha'er'a and Provincial Military Commander Hu Chao as deputies; soon Minister Wen Wei and Banner Commander Te Yishun replaced them as deputies.
translations.idiomatic: When the British invaded Zhejiang and Dinghai, Zhenhai, and Ningbo fell one after another, Yu Qian died in the fighting. Yijing was named Campaign General to lead the punitive force, with Ha'er'a and Hu Chao as deputies; before long Wen Wei and Te Yishun replaced them.

sentences.zh: 陛辭日，宣宗禦勤政殿，訓示方略，特詔：「申明軍紀，凡失守各城逃將逃兵，軍法從事。

translations.literal: On the day of his audience of leave, the Daoguang Emperor went to the Hall of Diligent Government and instructed him on strategy, with a special edict: "Make military discipline clear: all generals and soldiers who abandon their posts and flee from cities that fall shall be dealt with by military law."
translations.idiomatic: On the day he took leave of the throne, the Daoguang Emperor received him in the Hall of Diligent Government, laid out the strategy, and issued a special order: "Enforce discipline strictly: any commander or soldier who abandons a fallen city shall face the full penalty of military law."

sentences.zh: 」發交內庫花翎等件，有功者立予懋賞，勉以恩威並用，整飭戎行。

translations.literal: Peacock feathers and other items from the imperial treasury were issued; those with merit were to be rewarded at once with lavish honors, and he was exhorted to use both kindness and severity to put the army in order.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave him peacock feathers and other rewards from the palace stores, promising prompt honors for merit, and urged him to combine mercy and punishment and restore discipline in the ranks.

sentences.zh: 大學士穆彰阿奏請釋琦善出獄，隨赴軍前效力，奕經卻之。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Muzhanga memorialized to release Qi Shan from prison so he might serve at the front; Yijing refused.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Muzhanga asked that Qi Shan be freed from prison to serve at the front; Yijing declined.

sentences.zh: 奕經分屬懿親，素謹厚，為上所倚重，奉命專徵，頗欲有為而不更事，尤昧兵略。

translations.literal: Yijing was a close imperial kinsman, by nature cautious and solid, and was relied on by the emperor. Ordered on an independent campaign, he wished to accomplish much but lacked experience, and was especially ignorant of military strategy.
translations.idiomatic: As a senior imperial kinsman, Yijing was known for steadiness and enjoyed the emperor's trust. Given sole command of the campaign, he meant to achieve something but had little experience and knew almost nothing of war.

sentences.zh: 奏調陝甘、川、黔兵一萬人，請撥部餉一萬兩，倉猝未集，駐蘇州以待。

translations.literal: He memorialized to transfer ten thousand troops from Shaan-Gan, Sichuan, and Guizhou and requested ten thousand taels from the ministry treasury; they could not be gathered in haste, and he encamped at Suzhou to wait.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for ten thousand men from Shaanxi-Gansu, Sichuan, and Guizhou and ten thousand taels from the ministry treasury; nothing could be assembled quickly, so he halted at Suzhou to wait.

sentences.zh: 上以諸將少可恃者，命凡文武員弁及士民商賈有奇材異能一藝可取者，許詣軍前投效。

translations.literal: Because few of the generals could be relied on, the emperor ordered that any civil or military officer, scholar, commoner, or merchant with unusual talent or a useful skill might come to the army to offer service.
translations.idiomatic: Finding few generals trustworthy, the emperor allowed any official, scholar, commoner, or merchant with unusual talent or a useful skill to report to the army.

sentences.zh: 奕經渡江後，於營門設木匭，納名即延見，且許密陳得失。

translations.literal: After Yijing crossed the river he set up a wooden box at the camp gate; whoever submitted a name was received at once, and confidential statements of success or failure were permitted.
translations.idiomatic: After crossing the Yangzi, Yijing placed a wooden box at the camp gate: anyone who dropped in a name was summoned, and could speak freely in private about what was going right or wrong.

sentences.zh: 於是獻策者四百馀人，投效者一百四十馀人，而軍中所闢僚佐，多闒冗京員，投效者亦無異才。

translations.literal: More than four hundred then offered plans and more than one hundred forty came to serve, but the staff he recruited in the army were mostly idle Beijing officials, and those who came forward also had no exceptional talent.
translations.idiomatic: More than four hundred men offered advice and more than one hundred forty volunteered, yet the staff he gathered were mostly useless Beijing placemen, and the volunteers proved no better.

sentences.zh: 惟宿遷舉人臧紆青自負氣節，為言議撫徒損國威，始決主戰；

translations.literal: Only the Suqian licentiate Zang Shuqing, proud of his integrity, argued that to discuss peace would only harm national prestige, and only then did he decide to favor war;
translations.idiomatic: Only Zang Shuqing, a licentiate from Suqian proud of his integrity, persuaded him that talk of peace would only humiliate the dynasty, and at last Yijing resolved to fight;

sentences.zh: 又勸劾斬失律提督余步雲以立威望，疏具而旋寢。

translations.literal: he also urged impeachment and execution of the delinquent Provincial Military Commander Yu Buyun to establish authority; the memorial was drafted but then shelved.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged that the disgraced commander Yu Buyun be impeached and executed to restore morale; the memorial was written but then set aside.

sentences.zh: 以浙兵屢潰，不堪臨陣，召募山東、河南、安徽義勇。

translations.literal: Because Zhejiang troops repeatedly broke and could not face battle, he recruited militia from Shandong, Henan, and Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Since Zhejiang troops kept collapsing in battle, he raised militia from Shandong, Henan, and Anhui instead.

sentences.zh: 浙事日亟，巡撫劉韻珂促援，遲不至，遂相惡。

translations.literal: As the Zhejiang situation grew daily more urgent, Governor Liu Yunke pressed for aid, but help was slow in coming and they came to dislike each other.
translations.idiomatic: The crisis in Zhejiang worsened by the day; Governor Liu Yunke begged for reinforcements, but Yijing's army was slow to arrive, and the two men grew hostile.

sentences.zh: 久駐江蘇，以供應之累，官吏亦厭之，餉需文報，皆延擱不時應。

translations.literal: He remained long in Jiangsu; the burden of supply wearied the region, and officials also grew weary of him; pay, supplies, and documents were all delayed and not answered in time.
translations.idiomatic: He lingered in Jiangsu so long that supplying his army became a burden local officials resented; rations, funds, and paperwork were all held up.

sentences.zh: 十二月，始抵杭州。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he finally reached Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Only in the twelfth month did he reach Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 前泗州知州張應云獻策規复寧波，奕經、文蔚皆然之，遂令總理前敵營務。

translations.literal: The former prefect of Sizhou Zhang Yingyun offered a plan to recover Ningbo; Yijing and Wen Wei both approved, and he was ordered to take general charge of front-line camp affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yingyun, former prefect of Sizhou, proposed a plan to retake Ningbo; Yijing and Wen Wei both agreed, and put him in charge of front-line operations.

sentences.zh: 應云以重貲購寧波府吏陸心蘭為內應，日報機密多虛誑。

translations.literal: Zhang Yingyun used heavy payment to buy Ningbo clerk Lu Xinlan as an inside contact; his daily reports of secrets were mostly false.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yingyun bribed a Ningbo clerk named Lu Xinlan to act as an inside man; most of the intelligence he sent each day was empty boasting.

sentences.zh: 奕經禱於西湖關廟，占得「虎頭」之兆，乃議於二十二年正月寅日寅時進兵，屢遣諜，為敵所獲，漏師期。

translations.literal: Yijing prayed at the Guandi temple by West Lake and obtained the omen "tiger's head"; he then planned to advance on the yin day and yin hour of the first month of the twenty-second year, but spies he repeatedly sent were captured by the enemy and the time of attack was leaked.
translations.idiomatic: Yijing prayed at the Guandi temple on West Lake and drew the omen "tiger's head"; he then fixed an attack for the yin day and yin hour of the first month of the twenty-second year, but the spies he sent were caught and the battle plan leaked.

sentences.zh: 初，英兵踞府城僅二三百人，艦泊定海。

translations.literal: At first the English army held the prefectural city with only two or three hundred men, and their ships lay at Dinghai.
translations.idiomatic: At first the British held the prefectural city with only two or three hundred men while their fleet stayed at Dinghai.

sentences.zh: 至是，濮鼎查率十九艘兵二千散泊江岸，早為之備矣。

translations.literal: By then Pottinger had led nineteen ships and two thousand troops scattered along the riverbank and was long prepared.
translations.idiomatic: By then Pottinger had brought nineteen ships and two thousand troops, spread along the riverbanks, and was fully ready.

sentences.zh: 奕經由紹興進曹娥江，而慈谿敵兵退。

translations.literal: Yijing advanced from Shaoxing into the Cao'e River while the enemy at Cixi withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Yijing marched from Shaoxing up the Cao'e River as the British pulled back from Cixi.

sentences.zh: 應云請急進，遂駐慈谿東關，文蔚分屯長谿嶺，令提督段永福、余步雲等趨寧波，游擊劉天保趨鎮海，副將硃貴駐大寶山，而應云率所募義勇駐駱駝橋，為諸軍策應，約於正月晦數路並舉。

translations.literal: Zhang Yingyun asked for a rapid advance; they then encamped at the East Pass of Cixi while Wen Wei divided forces at Changxi Ridge, ordering Provincial Military Commanders Duan Yongfu and Yu Buyun and others toward Ningbo, Mobile Corps Commander Liu Tianbao toward Zhenhai, and Deputy Commander Zhu Gui at Great Treasure Hill, while Zhang Yingyun led the militia he had recruited at Camel Bridge to support the other columns, agreeing to strike together on several routes on the last day of the first month.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yingyun pressed for a quick advance. The army halted at Cixi's East Pass; Wen Wei held Changxi Ridge. Duan Yongfu, Yu Buyun, and others were sent toward Ningbo; Liu Tianbao toward Zhenhai; Zhu Gui took Great Treasure Hill; Zhang Yingyun camped at Camel Bridge with his hired militia to coordinate the columns. They planned a multi-pronged attack on the last day of the first month.

sentences.zh: 而敵已勾結應云部勇，勢且生變，不及待期，先二日輕軍分襲，不攜槍砲。

translations.literal: But the enemy had already won over men in Zhang Yingyun's militia and trouble was about to break out; unable to wait for the appointed day, two days early they sent light forces in separate raids without carrying muskets or cannon.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy had already suborned men in Zhang Yingyun's militia and an uprising was imminent. Unable to wait, they launched light detachments in separate raids two days early, without muskets or cannon.

sentences.zh: 永福等入寧波南門，中地雷，天保甫及鎮海城下，為敵砲擊退，皆大敗。

translations.literal: Yongfu and others entered Ningbo's south gate and struck land mines; Tianbao had only just reached the foot of Zhenhai's walls when enemy cannon drove him back—all suffered great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Yongfu's men entered Ningbo's south gate and hit land mines. Tianbao had barely reached Zhenhai when British guns drove him off. Every column was routed.

sentences.zh: 越日，應云所具火攻船為敵所焚，軍中自驚，奔大寶山。

translations.literal: The next day the fire-attack ships Zhang Yingyun had prepared were burned by the enemy; the army panicked on its own and fled to Great Treasure Hill.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the enemy burned Zhang Yingyun's fire ships. The army panicked and fled toward Great Treasure Hill.

sentences.zh: 硃貴收集潰兵圖進攻，敵兵已至，力戰竟日，殺傷相當，無援，貴死之。

translations.literal: Zhu Gui gathered the routed troops to attempt an attack; the enemy had already arrived; they fought fiercely all day with comparable casualties on both sides; without reinforcements, Gui died in the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Gui rallied the fugitives and tried to counterattack, but the enemy was already there. He fought all day with heavy losses on both sides; with no help coming, he was killed.

sentences.zh: 文蔚聞敗亦退，軍資器械棄失殆盡。

translations.literal: Wen Wei, hearing of the defeat, also withdrew; military stores and weapons were abandoned almost entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the defeat, Wen Wei withdrew as well, leaving nearly all supplies and weapons behind.

sentences.zh: 奕經留軍紹興，回駐杭州，自請嚴議，詔原之。

translations.literal: Yijing left troops at Shaoxing and returned to encamp at Hangzhou; he asked for severe punishment himself, and an edict pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Yijing kept part of the army at Shaoxing and returned to Hangzhou. He asked the court to punish him severely, but an edict let him off.

sentences.zh: 英艦乘勝由海窺錢塘江，以尖山海口淺阻，尋退去。

translations.literal: English ships, following up their victory, probed the Qiantang River from the sea, but the shallows at Jianshan barred them and they soon withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Victorious British ships probed the Qiantang from the sea, but the shallows at Jianshan blocked them and they soon withdrew.

sentences.zh: 鄭鼎臣者，殉難總兵國鴻子，曾從父軍。

translations.literal: Zheng Dingchen was the son of the martyred Regional Commander Guo Hong and had once followed his father's army.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Dingchen was the son of Guo Hong, the regional commander who died in battle, and had served under his father.

sentences.zh: 奕經予二十四萬金，令募水勇規复定海，聞寧鎮之敗，逡巡海上。

translations.literal: Yijing gave him 240,000 taels and ordered him to recruit naval braves to recover Dinghai; hearing of the defeats at Ningbo and Zhenhai, he lingered on the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Yijing gave him 240,000 taels to raise sailors and retake Dinghai, but after hearing of the Ningbo and Zhenhai disasters he hovered offshore without acting.

sentences.zh: 奕經督之嚴，乃報三月三日敗敵於定海十六門洋面，毀船數十，殲斃數百。

translations.literal: Under Yijing's stern pressure he then reported that on the third day of the third month he had defeated the enemy off Dinghai at the Sixteen Gates and destroyed several dozen ships, killing several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Pressed hard by Yijing, he reported that on the third day of the third month he had beaten the enemy off Dinghai at the Sixteen Gates, destroying dozens of ships and killing hundreds.

sentences.zh: 劉韻珂以為欺罔，奕經遣侍衛容照等出洋查勘，得焚毀船木及壞械回報，乃疏聞，賜奕經雙眼花翎，鼎臣亦被獎。

translations.literal: Liu Yunke considered this deception; Yijing sent Bodyguards Rong Zhao and others to inspect at sea, and they returned with burned ship timber and damaged weapons as evidence; he then memorialized the throne, and Yijing was granted the double-eyed peacock feather while Dingchen was also rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yunke called it a fraud, but Yijing sent guardsmen including Rong Zhao to investigate at sea; they brought back charred timbers and broken weapons. Yijing reported victory to the throne, received the double-eyed peacock feather, and Dingchen was rewarded too.

sentences.zh: 時寧波英兵忽退，留艦招寶山海口，改犯乍浦，陷之。

translations.literal: At that time the English troops in Ningbo suddenly withdrew, leaving ships at the mouth of Zhaobaoshan, and shifted to attack Zhapu, which fell.
translations.idiomatic: The British then suddenly left Ningbo, kept ships at Zhaobaoshan, turned on Zhapu, and captured it.

sentences.zh: 奕經不能赴援，而以收復寧波奏，詔斥不先事預防，革職留任。

translations.literal: Yijing could not go to relieve them, yet memorialized the recovery of Ningbo; an edict rebuked him for failing to take preventive measures beforehand and stripped his office while retaining him in his post.
translations.idiomatic: Yijing could not help Zhapu but reported Ningbo as recovered. The court rebuked him for lack of foresight, stripped his rank, and kept him on the job.

sentences.zh: 既而英兵犯江南，陷鎮江，逼江寧，命奕經赴援，尋命駐王江涇防禦。

translations.literal: Soon after the English army attacked Jiangnan, took Zhenjiang, and pressed Nanjing; Yijing was ordered to go to the relief, and soon after was ordered to encamp at Wangjiangjing on the defensive.
translations.idiomatic: The British then invaded Jiangnan, took Zhenjiang, and threatened Nanjing. Yijing was ordered to reinforce, then told to hold Wangjiangjing on the defensive.

sentences.zh: 奕經自寧波、慈谿之敗，軍心渙散，不能復用，益為劉韻珂所揶揄，議守議撫，一不使聞。

translations.literal: Since the defeats at Ningbo and Cixi, Yijing's army morale had dissolved and could not be used again; Liu Yunke mocked him all the more, and discussions of defense or pacification were kept from him entirely.
translations.idiomatic: After Ningbo and Cixi his army was useless and morale shattered. Liu Yunke ridiculed him openly and kept him out of every discussion of defense or peace.

sentences.zh: 及和議成，撤師，詔布奕經等勞師糜餉、誤國殃民罪狀，逮京論大辟。

translations.literal: When peace was concluded and troops withdrawn, an edict published the charges against Yijing and others of exhausting the army and treasury and harming the state and people; they were arrested and brought to the capital and sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: When peace came and the army was withdrawn, an edict listed Yijing's crimes—wasting troops and funds and bringing disaster on the country. He was taken to Beijing and sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 圈禁逾年，與琦善同起用，予四等侍衛，充葉爾羌幫辦大臣。

translations.literal: After more than a year in confinement he was reemployed together with Qi Shan, granted Fourth Class Bodyguard, and appointed Assistant Commissioner at Yarkand.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year under house arrest he was restored with Qi Shan, made a Fourth Class Bodyguard, and sent as assistant commissioner to Yarkand.

sentences.zh: 為御史陳慶鏞論劾，仍褫職。

translations.literal: Censor Chen Qingyong memorialized against him and he was again stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Chen Qingyong impeached him and he lost his post again.

sentences.zh: 未幾，复予二等侍衛，充葉爾羌參贊大臣，調伊犁領隊大臣。

translations.literal: Before long he was again granted Second Class Bodyguard, appointed Adviser Commissioner at Yarkand, and transferred to Brigade General of Ili.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Second Class Bodyguard again, adviser commissioner at Yarkand, then brigade general of Ili.

sentences.zh: 坐審鞫英吉沙爾領隊大臣齋清額誣捕良回獄不當，褫職發黑龍江。

translations.literal: For improperly trying Brigade General of Yengisar Zhai Qing'e on a charge of falsely arresting innocent Hui, he was stripped of office and sent to Heilongjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed and exiled to Heilongjiang for mishandling the trial of Zhai Qing'e, brigade general of Yengisar, who had been accused of falsely imprisoning innocent Muslims.

sentences.zh: 三十年，釋回。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he was released and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year he was freed and allowed to return.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，歷伊犁、英吉沙爾領隊大臣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianfeng he served successively as Brigade General of Ili and Yengisar.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianfeng he served in turn as brigade general of Ili and Yengisar.

sentences.zh: 二年，召授工部侍郎，調刑部，兼副都統。

translations.literal: In the second year he was summoned and appointed Vice Minister of Works, transferred to Punishments, and concurrently made Vice Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was recalled as vice minister of Works, moved to Punishments, and made vice commander-in-chief as well.

sentences.zh: 三年，命率密雲駐防赴山東防粵匪，卒於徐州軍次，依侍郎例賜卹。

translations.literal: In the third year he was ordered to lead the Miyun garrison to Shandong against the Cantonese rebels and died at the army camp in Xuzhou; condolence payments were granted according to the vice-minister precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was ordered to lead the Miyun garrison to Shandong against the Taiping rebels and died at Xuzhou on campaign; he received the standard vice-minister burial honors.

sentences.zh: =文蔚=文蔚，費莫氏，滿洲正藍旗人。

translations.literal: Wen Wei — Wen Wei, of the Feimo clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Wei — Wen Wei, of the Feimo clan, belonged to the Manchu Plain Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶二年進士，授翰林院檢討。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate in the second year of Jiaqing, he was appointed Hanlin Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the second year of Jiaqing and became a Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 累擢至兵部、工部侍郎，兼副都統、內務府大臣。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Vice Minister of War and Works, concurrently Vice Commander-in-Chief and Minister of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice minister of War and Works, and also served as vice commander-in-chief and minister of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 方其駐長谿嶺也，聞諸路軍皆不利，欲移營走。

translations.literal: While he was encamped at Changxi Ridge, hearing that every column had fared badly, he wished to move camp and flee.
translations.idiomatic: While he held Changxi Ridge and heard that every column had failed, he wanted to break camp and run.

sentences.zh: 敵雜難民潰兵猝至，焚毀營帳，乃奔曹娥江，收集潰兵，退保紹興。

translations.literal: The enemy mixed with refugees and routed troops arrived suddenly, burned the camp, and he fled to the Cao'e River, gathered the fugitives, and withdrew to defend Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: Enemy troops mixed with refugees and fugitives struck suddenly, burned his camp, and he fled to the Cao'e, rallied what he could, and fell back on Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 欲渡錢塘江，為劉韻珂所阻。

translations.literal: He wished to cross the Qiantang River but was blocked by Liu Yunke.
translations.idiomatic: He tried to cross the Qiantang but Liu Yunke stopped him.

sentences.zh: 尋以定海報捷，加頭品頂戴。

translations.literal: Soon, on the reported victory at Dinghai, he was given the ruby button of the first rank.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he received the first-rank ruby button for the reported victory at Dinghai.

sentences.zh: 軍事竣，追論失機，褫職下獄。

translations.literal: When military affairs ended, lost opportunities were pursued in review; he was stripped of office and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign ended he was prosecuted for missing his chance, stripped of rank, and jailed.

sentences.zh: 逾年，釋出，予三等侍衛，充古城領隊大臣，复褫職。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was released, granted Third Class Bodyguard, appointed Brigade General of Gucheng, and again stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was freed, made a Third Class Bodyguard and brigade general at Gucheng, then dismissed again.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，歷喀喇沙爾、哈密辦事大臣，駐藏大臣，奉天府尹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianfeng he served successively as Commissioner at Karashahr and Hami, Resident Commissioner in Tibet, and Prefect of Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianfeng he served as commissioner at Karashahr and Hami, imperial commissioner in Tibet, and prefect of Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 五年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year.

sentences.zh: =特依順=特依順，他塔喇氏，滿洲正藍旗人，福州駐防。

translations.literal: Te Yishun — Te Yishun, of the Tatara clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Blue Banner, stationed at Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Te Yishun — Te Yishun, of the Tatara clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Blue Banner on garrison duty at Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 累遷協領。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Battalion Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to battalion commander.

sentences.zh: 道光十三年，從平台灣張丙亂，擢荊州副都統。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Daoguang he joined the campaign against Zhang Bing's rebellion in Pingtaiwan and was promoted to Deputy Commander-in-Chief of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Daoguang he helped suppress Zhang Bing's rebellion in Pingtaiwan and was made deputy commander-in-chief of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 歷騰越鎮總兵、密雲副都統、寧夏將軍。

translations.literal: He served successively as Regional Commander of Tengyue, Deputy Commander-in-Chief of Miyun, and General of Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as regional commander of Tengyue, deputy commander-in-chief of Miyun, and military governor of Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，予都統銜，授參贊大臣，督師廣東。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was given the rank of Banner Commander, appointed Adviser Commissioner, and ordered to command troops in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he received banner-commander rank, became adviser commissioner, and was sent to command in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 尋命改赴浙江辦理軍務，駐守省城，署杭州將軍，遂實授。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered instead to go to Zhejiang to handle military affairs, garrison the provincial capital, act as General of Hangzhou, and then received the appointment in full.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon redirected to Zhejiang, garrisoned the provincial capital, acted as military governor of Hangzhou, and then received the post permanently.

sentences.zh: 乍浦陷，坐革職留任。

translations.literal: When Zhapu fell he was punished by stripping his office while retaining him in his post.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhapu fell he was demoted but kept at his post.

sentences.zh: 和議成，命籌辦浙江善後事宜。

translations.literal: When peace was concluded he was ordered to arrange Zhejiang's postwar affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After peace he was put in charge of Zhejiang's recovery.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，調烏里雅蘇台將軍。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was transferred to be General of Uliastai.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he was transferred to military governor of Uliastai.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，卒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-ninth year.

sentences.zh: =余步雲=余步雲，四川廣安人。

translations.literal: Yu Buyun — Yu Buyun was a native of Guang'an in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Buyun — Yu Buyun came from Guang'an in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶中，以鄉勇從剿教匪，積功至游擊。

translations.literal: During Jiaqing, as a local militiaman he joined the campaign against the White Lotus rebels and by accumulated merit rose to Mobile Corps Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jiaqing he joined the fight against the White Lotus rebels as a local militiaman and rose to mobile corps commander.

sentences.zh: 平瞻對叛番，累擢重慶鎮總兵。

translations.literal: He pacified the rebellious Tibetans of Zhandui and was repeatedly promoted to Regional Commander of Chongqing.
translations.idiomatic: He helped pacify the Zhandui rebellion and was promoted to regional commander of Chongqing.

sentences.zh: 道光七年，率本鎮兵從楊遇春徵回疆，破賊洋阿爾巴特莊；

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Daoguang he led his garrison troops under Yang Yuchun in the campaign in the Western Regions and defeated the rebels at Yang'a'erbat Village;
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Daoguang he led his garrison under Yang Yuchun into the Western Regions campaign and routed the rebels at Yang'a'erbat;

sentences.zh: 偕楊芳擊賊於毗拉滿，大敗之，復和闐，追擒賊酋玉努斯，授乾清門侍衛，擢貴州提督。

translations.literal: together with Yang Fang he attacked the rebels at Bilaman and routed them, recovered Khotan, pursued and captured the rebel chief Yunus, was appointed attendant of the Gate of Heavenly Purity, and promoted to Provincial Military Commander of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: with Yang Fang he smashed the rebels at Bilaman, retook Khotan, captured the rebel leader Yunus, became an attendant at the Gate of Heavenly Purity, and was made provincial military commander of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 調湖南。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Hunan.

sentences.zh: 十二年，率貴州兵剿江華瑤趙金龍，偕提督羅思舉破賊巢，金龍就殲，加太子少保。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he led Guizhou troops against the Yao Zhao Jinlong of Jianghua; together with Provincial Military Commander Luo Siju he destroyed the rebel lair and Jinlong was killed; he was given the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he led Guizhou troops against the Yao rebel Zhao Jinlong of Jianghua; with Luo Siju he destroyed the rebel base and killed Jinlong, and was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 复破粵瑤於永州藍山，擒其渠。

translations.literal: He again defeated the Cantonese Yao at Lanshan in Yongzhou and captured their leader.
translations.idiomatic: He also defeated Cantonese Yao rebels at Lanshan in Yongzhou and captured their chief.

sentences.zh: 從尚書禧恩赴廣東剿連州瑤，平之，賜雙眼花翎，予一等輕車都尉世職。

translations.literal: He followed Minister Xi'en to Guangdong to suppress the Yao of Lianzhou and pacified them; he was granted the double-eyed peacock feather and given the hereditary office of First Class Commandant of Light Chariots.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Minister Xi'en to Guangdong, pacified the Lianzhou Yao, received the double-eyed peacock feather, and was given the hereditary rank of First Class Commandant of Light Chariots.

sentences.zh: 歷四川、雲南提督，復調貴州。

translations.literal: He served successively as Provincial Military Commander of Sichuan and Yunnan and was again transferred to Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as provincial military commander of Sichuan and Yunnan in turn, then returned to Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 十八年，擒仁懷匪首謝法真，加太子太保，調福建提督。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he captured the bandit chief Xie Fazhen of Renhuai, was given the title Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and transferred to Provincial Military Commander of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he captured the bandit chief Xie Fazhen of Renhuai, was made Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and was posted to Fujian as provincial military commander.

sentences.zh: 二十年，英兵初陷定海，率師赴援，調浙江提督。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, when the English army first took Dinghai, he led troops to relieve them and was transferred to Provincial Military Commander of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, when the British first took Dinghai, he marched to relieve the city and was made provincial military commander of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，定海既收還，步雲駐防鎮海。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, after Dinghai had been recovered, Buyun garrisoned Zhenhai.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year, after Dinghai was recovered, Buyun was posted to defend Zhenhai.

sentences.zh: 裕謙來督師，疏言步云不可恃，未及易而英兵猝至，复陷定海，三鎮戰歿。

translations.literal: Yu Qian came to command the army and memorialized that Buyun could not be relied on; before he could be replaced the English army arrived suddenly, Dinghai fell again, and the three regional commanders died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qian arrived to command and reported that Buyun could not be trusted; before he could be replaced the British struck again, Dinghai fell, and three regional commanders were killed.

sentences.zh: 步雲屯招寶山，總兵謝朝恩分守金雞嶺。

translations.literal: Buyun encamped at Zhaobaoshan while Regional Commander Xie Chao'en separately defended Golden Cock Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Buyun held Zhaobaoshan while Regional Commander Xie Chao'en guarded Golden Cock Ridge.

sentences.zh: 步雲號宿將，實巧猾無戰志，又嗛裕謙剛愎，將戰，裕謙召與盟神誓師，託疾不赴，且獻緩敵之策。

translations.literal: Buyun was called a veteran general but was in fact cunning and slippery and had no will to fight; he also resented Yu Qian's stubbornness. When battle was imminent Yu Qian summoned him to swear an oath to the gods before the army; he pleaded illness and did not come, and offered a plan to slow the enemy instead.
translations.idiomatic: Buyun had a veteran's reputation but was sly and unwilling to fight, and he resented Yu Qian's stubbornness. When battle neared, Yu Qian called him to swear an oath before the troops; Buyun pleaded illness, stayed away, and urged delay instead.

sentences.zh: 敵攻其前，而以小舟載兵由石洞攀援登後山，步雲遽棄砲台走，敵乃據招寶山俯擊鎮海城，金雞嶺及縣城先後陷。

translations.literal: The enemy attacked in front while small boats carried troops up through stone caves to climb the rear hill; Buyun abruptly abandoned the battery and fled; the enemy then held Zhaobaoshan and struck down on Zhenhai city; Golden Cock Ridge and the county seat fell in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The British attacked from the front while small boats landed men through stone tunnels to scale the rear hill. Buyun abandoned his batteries and fled. The enemy took Zhaobaoshan and shelled Zhenhai from above; Golden Cock Ridge and the county seat soon fell.

sentences.zh: 步雲退寧波，敵掩至，墜馬傷足，僅免，府城遂陷。

translations.literal: Buyun withdrew to Ningbo; the enemy came up behind him; he fell from his horse and injured his foot, barely escaping, and the prefectural city then fell.
translations.idiomatic: Buyun fell back to Ningbo; the enemy overtook him; he was thrown from his horse, hurt his foot, and barely escaped as the city fell.

sentences.zh: 步雲疏聞，委敗於裕謙。

translations.literal: In his memorial Buyun laid the defeat at Yu Qian's door.
translations.idiomatic: In his report Buyun blamed the defeat on Yu Qian.

sentences.zh: 裕謙既歿，其妻赴京訟之。

translations.literal: After Yu Qian had died his wife went to the capital to bring suit against him.
translations.idiomatic: After Yu Qian's death his widow went to Beijing to accuse Buyun.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，從奕經規复寧波，不克，褫步雲職，逮京，命軍機大臣會刑部訊鞫。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he followed Yijing in the attempt to recover Ningbo and failed; Buyun was stripped of office, arrested and brought to the capital, and the Grand Councilors were ordered to join the Ministry of Punishments in interrogating him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he joined Yijing's failed attempt to retake Ningbo. Buyun was dismissed, taken to Beijing, and tried jointly by the Grand Council and the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 廷臣爭劾其罪，亦有原之者，獄久延，尚書李振祜堅持，讞乃定。

translations.literal: Court officials competed in impeaching his crimes, though some also pleaded for him; the case dragged on until Minister Li Zhenhu held firm and the verdict was finally fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Officials competed to denounce him, though some pleaded for mercy. The trial dragged on until Minister Li Zhenhu held firm and the sentence was fixed.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「餘步雲膺海疆重寄，未陣獲一賊，身受一傷，首先退縮，以致將士效尤，奔潰棄城，直同兒戲。

translations.literal: An edict stated: "Yu Buyun bore heavy responsibility on the coast; before battle he captured not a single enemy; though he received one wound, he was the first to shrink back, so that officers and soldiers followed his example, fled in rout, and abandoned cities—as if it were child's play."
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: "Yu Buyun held a grave coastal command. He captured no enemy in battle, took one wound, and was the first to retreat. Officers and men followed his example, routed, and abandoned their cities—as if war were a game."

sentences.zh: 儻不置之法，不惟無以肅軍政而振人心，且何以慰死節諸臣於地下？

translations.literal: If he is not punished by law, not only will military government and popular morale fail to be restored, but how can the officials who died loyal be comforted beneath the earth?
translations.idiomatic: If he is not punished, how can discipline be restored or the people heartened—and how can the loyal dead be honored in their graves?

sentences.zh: 」步雲遂棄市。

translations.literal: Buyun was then executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Buyun was then executed.

sentences.zh: =【論】=論曰：奕山、奕經，天潢貴冑，不諳軍旅，先後棄師，如出一轍，事乃益不可為。

translations.literal: Commentary: Yishan and Yijing were noble imperial kin, unversed in military affairs; they abandoned their armies in succession in the same manner, and affairs became all the more impossible.
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: Yishan and Yijing were imperial princes who knew nothing of war. Each in turn abandoned his army in the same way, and the situation grew hopeless.

sentences.zh: 其人皆庸闇不足責，當時廷臣不能預計，疆吏不能匡救，可謂國無人焉。

translations.literal: The men themselves were mediocre and dim and not worth blaming; at the time court officials could not foresee, and frontier governors could not correct—the state, it may be said, had no capable men.
translations.idiomatic: The men were too mediocre to blame alone; court officials could not foresee the crisis and frontier governors could not set things right. One might say the empire had no one fit for the task.

sentences.zh: 奕山後復棄東北邊地，其貽患尤深。

translations.literal: Yishan later again abandoned the northeastern frontier lands, and the harm he left was especially deep.
translations.idiomatic: Yishan later surrendered the northeastern frontier as well, and the damage he left was even worse.

sentences.zh: 餘步雲庸懦巧猾，卒膺顯戮。

translations.literal: Yu Buyun was mediocre, cowardly, and cunning, and in the end suffered public execution.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Buyun was mediocre, cowardly, and cunning, and in the end was publicly executed.

sentences.zh: 宣宗於僨事諸人，皆從寬典，伸軍律者，僅步雲一人耳。

translations.literal: The Daoguang Emperor treated all those involved in the defeat with lenient measures; only Buyun alone had military law enforced against him.
translations.idiomatic: The Daoguang Emperor treated nearly everyone involved in the disaster leniently; only Buyun was punished under military law.
